newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain cut now expected after 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain cut now expected after 1997 budget.

text.p: Spanish financial markets shrugged aside the Bank of Spain's decision on Tuesday to withhold a reduction in its key money market rate, confident it will cut at the next repo, after the 1997 budget presentation.

"It was pretty clear Bank of Spain would wait for the budget draft. The only problem was with the peseta strength but they overcame it with intervention," said Alfredo Urrutia, chief economist with Societe Generale in Madrid.
The government is set to present its budget draft next Monday, and the Bank of Spain is expected to respond with a cut in its 7.25 percent money market rate at its subsequent tender, on October 3.
"The Bank of Spain will need to applaud the budget draft," said Henrik Lumholdt, economist with Bank of America in Madrid.
"We were awaiting a rate cut today or on October 3, " said Carmen Hernansanz, analyst at Merrill Lynch, who now forecasts a 25 basis point cut in the 7.25 percent official rate next week.
Economists said they are convinced the market is already discounting a 25 basis point cut on the short end, and they suspect the Bank of Spain will not be any more generous than that.
"The Bank of Spain is not really convinced the budget is tight enough and they do not think the economy needs more," said Lumholdt. "I do not see any urgency for them to do more".
The inflation trend also suggests the Bank of Spain will remain sparing in its reduction, analysts said.
"The inflation trend is doing fine. We do believe end-year data can be below 3.5 percent, but still there is no reason to exaggerate," said Hernansanz.
The Bank of Spain had said it was concerned about the recent rise in unit labour costs.
"I'm not worried about it. I think it a kind of compensation for what the employees lost during the past," said Lumholdt, but "Bank of Spain is closely watching it."
A Reuter poll on Monday showed that five of 10 economists were expecting a 25 basis point rate cut today. But the market reaction to the Bank of Spain's announcement was positive.
The peseta was trading almost unchanged at 0920 GMT at 84.16/19 versus the mark, while the December future contract on ten-year bonos was up 22 basis points at 105.47.
The December Mibor contract was trading at 93.26, unchanged from yesterday.
